text:
noah: Hey payroll team — I moved from CA to WA on 2025-09-10 and my 09/25 paycheck still shows CA state tax withheld (~$420). WA has no income tax. Can someone check my tax residency flag?

jen-payroll: Thanks for the ping Noah. Did you update your address in Workday and submit a new state withholding form (if applicable)?

noah: I updated my Workday address on 2025-09-11 and uploaded a WA address proof (lease). I submitted a new state withholding election in the portal on 2025-09-12. I see CA on the paystub line item though.

sam-peopleops: @noah we'll open a payroll ticket. Often the payroll system keeps the original state for the run if the change was after the cutoff. We need to check whether the CA tax was applied because the pay period covered earnings while you were still CA resident. Can you confirm your last CA workday?

noah: Last CA workday was 2025-09-09. Pay period was 09/01-09/15 and payday 09/25. So the pay covers mostly work when I was in CA but final paycheck period includes days after move.

jen-payroll: Got it. Two things we'll check: 1) residency vs source-of-income rules for CA (part-year resident) and 2) whether the payroll run applied state withholding based on pay period start date. I'll create PR-4890.

payroll-bot: PR-4890 created by jen-payroll. Status: investigating. Priority: medium.

jen-payroll: If CA withholding was correct for earnings while resident, we may still owe CA tax on that portion. If withholding covers earnings after your move, we can request a refund/adjustment with our vendor or provide a supplemental calculation so you can claim a credit on your WA filing (WA has no income tax so credit not applicable, but helpful for record).

noah: Ideally I'd rather not be double-taxed once states reconcile. Will the company pursue an employer-side correction if it was a payroll cutoff issue?

sam-peopleops: Yes — if withholding was applied in error for post-move earnings, we'll ask the vendor for a retro adjustment and corrected state withholding records. If it was correct for pay earned while you were CA resident, we'll produce a detailed earnings breakdown so you can file a part-year CA return claiming only CA-source income.

intl-vendor: PR-4890 received. We're checking the payrun mapping for employee 77421. Preliminary: the tax-state field was set to CA for the 09/25 run because the effective address change landed after the vendor cutoff. We'll confirm whether the CA withholding amount includes days after 09/09. ETA: 5 business days.

jen-payroll: Operational plan we put in PR-4890: 1) request vendor report showing state withholding by pay-date for the pay period, 2) if post-move earnings were taxed, request a refund/adjustment and corrected state reporting, 3) if adjustment isn't possible before filing season, provide an employer statement with itemized earnings and withheld CA tax.

noah: Thanks. One question  will this change my W-2? I want to make sure I file correctly for 2025.

jen-payroll: If we issue any retro corrections that affect year-to-date withholding, we may issue a corrected W-2 (W-2c) or provide a payroll statement reflecting the adjustment. We'll update PR-4890 when we know vendor timelines.

payroll-bot: PR-4890 update: vendor confirmed cutoff cause. Refund request submitted on 2025-10-03. Next update expected 10-17-2025. Owner: jen-payroll.

noah: Appreciate it 64F. I uploaded lease + move confirmation to the ticket. Happy to provide any other docs if needed.
